Aisha: Heads-up: ran a parity probe comparing emulation vs prod traces for the kernel selection change. Initial mismatch numbers look higher for long sequences.
Tom B: What's off — latency or output mismatch rate?
Aisha: Mismatch rate ~1.8% for traces >2k tokens when we enable the new batching heuristic + kernel fallback. KV-cache hit patterns diverge early.
Ravi: Can you share the probe config (sampler, anon seed, concurrency)? Need exact params to reproduce deterministically.
Aisha: Config we used:
```
sampler: stratified_by_session_length
strata: [short, medium, long]
anon_seed: 42
trace_scrub: timestamps->offsets, user_ids->hashes
concurrency: 8
batching: heuristic_v2
kernel_selection: runtime_auto
kv_eviction: lru
```
Claire: If anon_seed or scrub rules differ parity will blow up. Also confirm you didn't preserve absolute timestamps anywhere.
Aisha: I stripped absolute ts -> relative offsets. Sampler was 1% stratified (biased toward long sessions). Replay concurrency 8. My hypothesis: batching ordering + kernel fallback causes different KV warmup ordering => early evictions and state mismatch.
Tom B: Let's run apples-to-apples: pin the kernel and disable heuristic batching, identical anonymization & sampler. Compare token-level parity and perf. Also capture per-step KV checksums and kernel selection logs.
Aisha: Running with this command next:
```
./tools/replay \ 
  --trace=/mnt/traces/2026-03-15-scrubbed.tgz \ 
  --anon-seed=42 \ 
  --concurrency=8 \ 
  --pin-kernel=gpt-opt-1 \ 
  --batching=off \ 
  --dump-kv-checksums=kv_checks_run1.json \ 
  --dump-kernel-decisions=kernel_log_run1.txt \ 
  --out=run1.log
```
perf-bot: run queued 2481234705 by Aisha :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Ravi: Add `--dump-kernel-decisions` (nice), and `--force-kv-deterministic-evict` if available to test eviction ordering. Also watch for a kernel switch at ~step 2100 in older logs.
Aisha: Good call — enabling deterministic-evict flag now. I'll share checksums and kernel logs when complete. If parity discrepancy remains, next step is to make KV eviction deterministic relative to batch ordering or to add a prewarm pass that fills cache in canonical order.
Tom B: Sounds good. If the pinned kernel run matches, we know kernel auto-selection + batching ordering is the culprit. If it still differs, then anonymization/sampling subtlety remains. Keep us posted.
Claire: :thumbsup: thanks for the quick triage.
Aisha: Will post results in this thread— starting run now.
